findings.issue: When `tail` starts with a JSON object but the restart isn’t longer than the kept findings, `stitched` is never assigned, leading to an UnboundLocalError later.

findings.issue: The `render_md` function calculates a percentage using integer division, which is safe due to the `if summary['real']` check, but it could be cleaner.
The `ledger_block` function imports `hare_ledger` inside the function to avoid circular imports. This is a standard workaround but worth noting.

Resolved threads are keyed by path only, then every still-open finding on that path is marked `resolved`. The GraphQL query already selects `line`, and that field is unused. One resolved Hare thread on a file (including a thread resolved because the line left the diff) changes the fate of every other open finding on the same file. Those fates feed the hit rate and the prompt line that says not to raise a resolved finding again. `test_pr_rows_follows_a_finding_from_note_to_note` has only one finding on `scripts/b.py`, so the path-wide match stays green.

`note_meta` only reads a Models row whose slug is in backticks. The ledger committed here has 72 notes and 17 hops. Older notes still use `**ship** · \`slug\` · effort low` (the notes on #221 are that shape), so the hop table does not say which hop answered for most notes.
`gh pr create` is followed by `|| echo`, so any create failure, not only an already-open PR, leaves the step green after the force-push.

findings.issue: The reasoning-knob retry calls `_post` outside the `HTTPError` wrapper. A second 400/404/422 escapes as a bare `HTTPError` (`HTTP Error 400: bad` with no body), so the nag loses the cause on the path this PR adds to name errors.
Every Nous hop is pinned to `effort: none`. That is the fast pass. Right for ending empty answers; the usual good review still wants reasoning on when the provider can return content.
`nous` now sends a reasoning knob, but the `HARE_NOUS_DEFAULT` comment above still says Nous hops carry no reasoning control and uses that to justify putting space-bunny last.
The PR body says 'Job timeout 20 → 25 min' and claims 'the existing test checks the sum', but the diff sets 30 and no test asserts the workflow timeout.
The comment says the budget 'has to hold two hung hops and still reach a live one', but 2 × 300 s = 600 s = the entire budget, so a third hop never starts.
The new budget comment says two full hangs spend the 600 s budget, which contradicts the intended guarantee that the budget should hold two hung hops and still allow a live hop.
The model‑list comment was re‑phrased but now splits a sentence across lines, reducing readability.

entries.title: fix(hare): make the reasoning hop answer, and stop losing the answer

findings.issue: The fence regex uses `\\` (literal backslash) instead of triple backticks. The fence path is dead code; the test passes only because `json_objects` covers the same case. A future maintainer who trusts the fence path will be surprised.

`test_hare_once_accepts_an_ordered_hop_override` inspects `co_varnames` rather than calling the function with a `hop_override` and asserting the provider list is honoured. It will pass even if the parameter is ignored at runtime.

Setting `os.environ["GITHUB_EVENT_NAME"]` mutates the process globally. If any imported module reads that variable at import time or in a later call, it will see the spoofed value. A `contextlib` or explicit parameter would be safer, but the current scope (single script, single call) makes the risk low.

This is the body the Groq hop receives. The Action pins `openai/gpt-oss-120b`. Groq's knob is top-level `reasoning_effort`, and for gpt-oss the allowed values are low, medium, and high (`none` is Qwen-only). A nested `reasoning` object is the OpenRouter shape this file already says Gemini must not use. If Groq ignores it, the first hop stays on default medium reasoning and can spend the hop budget before Nous, which is the hop the writeup measured. If Groq rejects it, the first hop 400s. The tests that pin `{"reasoning": {"effort": "none"}}` for Groq have to move with the fix. Zen is given the same unmeasured object, and the Action sends no Zen key.

The fence pattern matches backslashes, not markdown fences, so that branch never sees a fenced JSON block. Brace scanning still finds a simple object inside the fence, which is why the fence test stays green. (already raised in a thread)

This line says both arms ran on the same PRs. Thinking on is 231, 233, 227, 230, 221, 224. Thinking off is 234, 224, 222, 221, 223, 217, 218. Only 221 and 224 sit in both. The six empty thinking-on runs still stand. The pairing does not.

The new `except TimeoutError` does not see a urllib timeout. `urlopen` wraps that timeout in `urllib.error.URLError`, so the named "LLM timeout after Ns" message never runs. The hop loop still catches the URLError and moves on.
`--model` and the default key walk only know nous, zen, and openrouter, so the local loop cannot run the Groq or Gemini hops the Action tries first. (already raised in a thread)
`test_hare_once_accepts_an_ordered_hop_override` only checks that the name `hop_override` exists. It stays green if the parameter is ignored. (already raised in a thread)
The module doc shows `--skip-checks`. The parser only has `--wait-checks`, and skipping checks is already the default. (already raised in a thread)
The new docstring contains a real tab and a form feed, so it reads "in ext" and "a ind". (already raised in a thread)
